transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-01
Time: 10:00 AM - 11:15 AM PDT
Duration: ~75 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Jordan, Priya, Alex, Elena, Samir, Tess
Links shared: Q4 roadmap deck (link), launch-checklist-v2 (internal doc), incident-2026-09-28-postmortem (link), perf-replay.csv (sheet)

[00:00] Maya: okay, let's get started — thanks everybody for carving time. main goal today is to make sure we're launch-ready for the Q4 featureset, and go through the incident from last week so we don't repeat it.
[00:20] Jordan: yeah, I forwarded the perf logs and the replay dataset earlier, uh sorry if the email hit late.
[00:28] Priya: I pulled the SLO graphs, we've got the tail latency spikes during the deploy window, looks like KV cache thrash when we rolled the runtime.
[00:35] Samir: quick context — that deploy was the quantization rollout on dedicated. It was a canary but the canary size wasn't isolated enough.
[00:45] Tess: QA saw a flakiness spike in the regression suite as well, a lot of the end-to-end tests that mock long sequences failed intermittently.

[01:05] Maya: okay, incident review first — Priya, can you summarize root cause and immediate remediation?
[01:12] Priya: yeah, so root cause appears to be a mismatch in kernel selection for the quantized path plus a cache invalidation timing issue under heavy concurrency. basically the runtime picked a slightly different conv kernel that caused higher memory pressure and evicted KV entries. when KV is missing we fall back to full recompute and latency jumps.
[01:35] Jordan: there's also an orchestration detail — autoscaler put extra pods up simultaneously, which combined with the kernel switch increased pressure. should've been a rolling update with slower ramp.
[01:48] Maya: got it. so remediation items?
[01:50] Priya: immediate stop-gap was to rollback the quantization profile for that cluster, that dropped the error rate back to baseline. long-term we need kernel pinning for canaries and better cache warming.
[02:05] Jordan: and a stricter deploy policy for Dedicated — change the default canary percent to 5% and require verification window of 30 minutes before ramp.

[02:25] Elena: question — do we need an engineering change to the runtime to support kernel pinning, or can orchestration handle it?
[02:32] Jordan: short answer — orchestration can constrain variants, but kernel pinning likely needs a small runtime flag so we can force a specific kernel for a rollout. it's a small change but touches the compilation path.
[02:45] Maya: add to action items: Jordan to scope kernel pinning change and estimate.

[03:05] Maya: now roadmap checkpoints — status of the Q4 feature list: model routing improvements, canary tooling, pricing telemetry, and rollback automation. Jordan, what's the status on model routing?
[03:18] Jordan: model routing's mostly on track, we've got an initial MVP to route by latency SLO and cost tier. We still need to hook in the fallback policy for model variants and test cross-region fallbacks.
[03:32] Alex: from design perspective we need to update the Console UI for per-route dashboards so PMs can toggle fallbacks easily. current mocks are in the drive.
[03:40] Maya: UX is critical for SREs during incidents. Alex, make sure the toggles are discoverable.

[04:00] Tess: QA status: we have ~80% coverage for happy path, but low coverage for long-sequence streaming and burst concurrency. I need 2 more test scenarios to reach the target.
[04:12] Maya: what's blocking those tests?
[04:15] Tess: we need a stable replay dataset that represents prod tail traffic and an updated test harness that can simulate and measure KV hit rates.
[04:25] Jordan: I can generate the replay subset and wire it into the harness; that'll also feed into the perf bench.

[04:40] Maya: timeline check — we want to start the canary for the feature set next week, so everything should be green by 2026-10-07. is that still realistic?
[04:49] Samir: with the kernel pinning and stricter canary percent probably yes, but we need the bench results to be confident.

[05:05] (brief cross-talk)
[05:20] Priya: on the incident follow-ups, I'll own the postmortem doc — I'll add the timeline, RCA, and remediation plan. also will list detectable signals for the alerting runbook.
[05:32] Maya: speak to the runbook — we need runbook steps added to Console so oncall can initiate rollback steps quickly. Alex, can you add a small UI entry point to the incident page?
[05:42] Alex: yeah, I'll add a deploy rollback CTA and a checklist link.

[06:00] Jordan: perf bench plan — I'll run end-to-end benchmarks on the q4-replay dataset with the quantized and non-quantized branches, with canary percent set to 5% in a test cluster, and capture tail p95/p99 and KV hit ratio.
[06:18] Maya: great, include cold-starts and long-seq streaming. make sure we report token/sec and cost-per-token estimates for Dedicated vs Hosted.

[06:35] Elena: on compliance and security items — any changes that affect data retention or KMS?
[06:42] Priya: not for this deploy. we are not changing retention or KMS configs. kernel pinning doesn't touch keys. still, we'll iterate with security for the canary plan if we change logging levels.

[07:00] (15-minute marker summary)
[07:10] Maya: quick recap — incident RCA: kernel selection + autoscaler ramp causing KV thrash. Remediations: rollback (done), kernel pinning, stricter canary percent, cache warming. Action owners assigned. Roadmap: model routing, canary tooling, pricing telemetry, rollback automation. QA gaps: long-seq and burst tests. Bench to run by Friday.

[07:45] Samir: one more ask — can we get a small budget for additional Dedicated capacity for the canary window? the current pool is heavily utilized and giving us noisy neighbors.
[07:58] Maya: request noted; I'll escalate to infra budget owners, but for now try to schedule canary in low-util windows.

[08:20] Tess: about rollback automation — QA will write the scenarios that need to trigger an automatic rollback (degraded p99, error rate). we need the guardrails spelled out otherwise it'll flip too aggressively.
[08:35] Jordan: agree. rollback automation should be gated behind manual opt-in first with a two-tier threshold.

[09:00] (discussion of rollout schedule, tentative dates, and docs to share)
[09:15] Maya: final next steps: I'll update the launch checklist and share; Jordan runs perf bench; Priya finalizes postmortem; Tess finalizes QA matrix; Alex adds UI CTA for runbook. we'll reconvene Fri 2026-10-02 for a quick sync after bench results.
[09:40] Elena: quick note — also prepare a short internal communication for CS and sales about potential limited availability during canary. keep it short.
[09:50] Maya: good call. I'll draft and share.

[10:05] (wrap up)
[10:10] Maya: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: some technical terms were auto-corrected (kv cache sometimes appears as "k v cash"), proper nouns may be off. Timestamp spacing is approximate and aligns to conversation pace.
